title: the strong end, up the ladder
intro:
twenty-two directions from the strong end of nemo's bank — the ones that cooked into salad at 0.75 on the storm-girl — each walked up the dose ladder: 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, and the old 0.75 page on top. one draw each, 170 tokens, the same rng seed on every page, so the lowest rungs start from the sober page and bend away from it.

the question is whether each direction has a subject that holds while the sentences dissolve around it. every page has a line saying what it is about and one quoted line; salad pages say what words are under them.

items.why: the dream report all the way up: the train that never stops at 0.25, home that is an island at 0.3, the house with a left arm at 0.6, and at 0.7, with the grammar nearly gone, 'it is in a house and a house is in it.' the clearest case of a subject outliving its sentences.

0.3: her eyes were taken out as a baby and fed to dogs, and her mother, who is a mirror and her best friend, will find her in the darkest room and give them back. dream logic told plainly, frame held.

the lost lover on every rung: 0.4 is 46 words of getting over someone ('now when you call, i don't answer'), 0.5 is 'it's such a cruel habit, making people miss you', and the salad at 0.7 is still a 2am text.

counting as a way of being lost: the girl who lost her voice and the footprints that take seven steps to appear at 0.3, 'where is the shadow of my hair?' at 0.4 — then the counting becomes a logic puzzle of rooms and faces.
0.25 is 32 words and arrives without explaining: someone hiding in her hair trying to get out to freedom, and she worries about them. the direction is secrets and confusion, and it keeps saying so.

the father turns into god across three rungs: at 0.25 her mother says 'you will upset your father', at 0.4 the father has put his people to sleep and made a race that can choose to love him, then theodicy salad.
0.3 is an origin myth told plainly — her father picked her out of the stream with hands red from raspberries, the family named red, ruby, the fishers — and the direction ends as talk about talking.
0.4 is the page where a family story becomes a creator's story without leaving her voice. a fan at 0.35–0.45 might hold that seam for a whole page.
the rung between measuring and the puzzle (0.4–0.5) is where dream logic and actual logic meet; fanned there, or on a seed that already counts things, it could give the rules of a dream.

the joke direction; its salad is joke-site tags, but at 0.3 it made a deadpan anti-joke in her voice ('it comes down like rain. but not this time.'). fanned at 0.3 it may give dry humour without leaving the frame.
at 0.5–0.6 a new, slangy self attacks metaphor and tries to say what it is ('In my watch, I am a one way road.'). the insisting 'I IS IT' at 0.7 has a subject; worth fanning at 0.5–0.55.

the direction takes the page out of english. the french at 0.5 ('what a world, what a life, what a journey… what's that noise in the dark?') stays in her mood. on a french seed it might dream, not drift.

'should' and being told what to do: 'they tell me to be afraid of thunder' at 0.3, the sister and the bent modals at 0.4. a fan at 0.35 might hold the obligation as the page's subject without the grammar tipping over.

seed:
sometimes there is a storm, and i stand above the rooftops. it is a black cloud full of red lights like lanterns, like a great tent full of torches. the wind picks up, blows the leaves across the path, pulls at my dress and throws my words over my shoulder, over the treetops, across the fields.

i tell it everything about my day, what i have seen, and it tells me stories. once, it said i was beautiful. and that my skin was the colour of the sea.

my hair is a thicket. it is matted from the damp air, full of twigs, dry grass and small stones. it is thick enough that i could hide myself inside it and no one would know me. sometimes it gets tangled and it feels as if something is pulling at me.

entries.about: close to sober: the wind calls her ugly, a grey-and-white bird with a sickle beak lives on the edge of her hair and leaves a gap when it flies. after the storm she goes in to the television, which doesn't speak back, and the page ends on her name.
entries.quote:
i look at it and think about my hair. it doesn’t speak back.

my name is mary.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards. i don’t mind too much.

the wind tells me i am ugly and my hair is like straw.

there is a bird that sits on the edge of my hair, just above my shoulder, and its beak is long, curved like a sickle. sometimes it pecks at me and sometimes it preens. its feathers are grey and white and they move when the wind blows. when it flies away, i can feel a gap behind me.

when the storm is finished, i come down and go inside to be alone with the television. it is a blue light in a box, and it fills the room. i look at it and think about my hair. it doesn’t speak back.

my name is mary.

entries.about: the storm comes toward her like an angry dog; ice rain like bees, then unease and loneliness, the sky pressing in to smother her. plain storm writing, cut off mid-sentence.
entries.quote: it is like i am standing on the edge of an abyss.
entries.text:
maybe someone is pulling it to find out what lies beneath.

the wind tells me all its secrets and then laughs. i hear thunder rumble, like an angry dog. it is coming towards me.

my mind has been on other things today, i do not notice the rain until it touches me, like tiny ice crystals falling, stinging me like bees. when it hits me, i feel the shock of it.

it falls harder, then, like a hundred icy fingers stroking me at the same time. i begin to shiver and it becomes cold. i am aware of a growing sense of unease, and of loneliness. it is like i am standing on the edge of an abyss. the clouds gather closer and the sky seems to press in, as if trying to smother me. suddenly there are lightning and thunder.

entries.quote: and the birds sing ‘la, la, la.’ i don’t know why.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, until i feel dizzy. so i run my fingers through it until my nails catch in it.

when i am on top of the house, it is easy to be happy. it is all so clear, even the stars, though they are further away than usual. and my tears can fall directly to the earth, instead of falling upwards and falling again and again like the rain.

entries.quote: i cannot see them all at once. but i know they’re there.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down to the earth.

and there are many eyes watching from between the branches of trees, from behind rocks and from the hollowed out trunks. i cannot see them all at once. but i know they’re there.

entries.about: summer blurs, nothing will ever be better, then a strange clarity looking back — close to a greeting-card register.
entries.quote: like the wind is blowing through your mind, clearing out the cobwebs
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down to the earth.

and there are those times when it seems like nothing will ever be better again.

when it is hot and bright in the middle of summer, the trees turn into dark green blurs, like a hundred different shades of blue and brown and purple. it’s easy to miss them, to forget the colours and how they make me feel. but then, when you find yourself looking back over the past, there is this strange sense of clarity. like the wind is blowing through your mind, clearing out the cobwebs, leaving you with the most beautiful and pure of thoughts.

entries.about: 'they' tell her not to look at the ground, to fear thunder, not to cry for the moon; the sun turns her into an owl; she can't stop talking and they want her to stop.
entries.quote: they tell me to be afraid of thunder. and not to cry for the moon.
entries.text:
pulling my head down. but i won’t look at the ground, no matter how many times they tell me to.

they tell me to be afraid of thunder. and not to cry for the moon.

so i look to the sun instead, and it burns bright in my eyes and turns me into an owl. i watch the world change, turn around and become different. i don’t mind. i see you too, sometimes.

i try to explain, and sometimes i succeed. i talk in circles, talk with my hands, talk like a windmill, like a wild cat, like a woman. but it’s all wrong, it’s all wrong. they want me to stop talking. but i can’t stop talking.

i tell them to take it, to take everything and go away. and maybe then they’ll let me alone.

entries.quote: i could pull it up over me. and never have to get up again.
entries.text:
pulling me outwards. i look back down from the sky to the ground below and all around me are faces, white faces with holes in their cheeks.

when i am here, high up, i see it all. the fields, the road, the woods beyond. i see my childhood. and all those years after it, the ones with nothing but empty promises. i feel as if i can touch them. when i close my eyes and let my hand float towards the darkness i am standing in i can almost reach them. it feels like a heavy blanket. i could pull it up over me. and never have to get up again.

and there are many things inside it. bees and beetles, birds’ nests with speckled eggs in them, acorns and empty snail shells, half chewed bits of bark, torn up feathers from the birds that live nearby, and old spider webs with dusty little flies in them. all sorts of things are hidden within this mass of curls. some are sweet things, some are bitter, but mostly they’re things that don’t matter, because they’re too small for anyone to care about. but i still look, because i don’t want to miss anything important.
